description: The Blackwater Canyon Trail is part of a broader network that allows users to explore the diverse and historically rich areas around the lower Blackwater River. The trail starts at the Blackwater Crossing Recreation Site, and there are various options for trail users from this point. People looking for a short hike can complete a small "there and back" circuit of about 3km which leads to the edge of the river. More adventurous hikers can choose to complete larger loops, choosing to either return back to the original starting point or link up the Alexander Mackenzie Heritage Trail parking area on the Blackwater Road (about 12-15km round trip depending on the route). The longer loops pass through beautiful open Douglas Fir forests and offer stunning views of the Blackwater River along the way.
directions: Head west of Prince George to the Blackwater Road, and travel until the road turns to gravel at the Baldy Hughes therapeutic community. Continue along the gravel portion of the Blackwater Road for approximately 42 kilometres. The site is located on the left side of the road, immediately before the bridge over the Blackwater River
title: Blackwater Canyon
